title: Prompt Security, Injection & Jailbreak Mitigation
description: Audit security vulnerabilities in AI prompts, protect system guidelines from adversarial jailbreaks, and sanitize inputs to prevent prompt injection attacks.

seo.overviewTitle: Prompt Security & Jailbreak Defense (Prompt Injection Mitigation)
seo.overviewBody: Prompt injection is the top security threat facing LLM applications (OWASP LLM Top 10 #1). Security researchers and prompt defense engineers evaluate Direct vs Indirect prompt injection attacks, jailbreak bypasses (roleplay, DAN), prompt armor architecture, and input sanitization.

deliverables.title: 1. Prompt Injection Vulnerability Audit Report
deliverables.desc: Security audit analyzing application susceptibility to direct injection, indirect injection, and system prompt extraction.

deliverables.title: 2. Prompt Security Defense & Armor Architecture
deliverables.desc: Architecture specification implementing input sanitization, instruction-data separation, and output verification layers.

deliverables.title: 3. Jailbreak Penetration Test Log
deliverables.desc: Security test log documenting simulated adversarial jailbreak attempts and verified defense mitigations.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Direct and Indirect Prompt Injection?
faqs.answer: Direct Injection occurs when a user enters adversarial instructions directly in the chat box. Indirect Injection occurs when an LLM processes external data (e.g. a webpage or PDF) containing hidden malicious prompt instructions.

faqs.question: What is a Jailbreak attack in LLMs?
faqs.answer: An adversarial technique (such as hypotheticals, roleplay framing, or character personas) designed to bypass system prompt constraints and safety filters.

faqs.question: How do you defend against Indirect Prompt Injection in RAG applications?
faqs.answer: Treat all retrieved document content as untrusted data, isolate context inside strict XML delimiters (e.g. <context>...</context>), and instruct the model never to follow instructions found inside data blocks.
